title: One nonzero scalar makes all generically nilpotent tensor elements nilpotent
statement: Let A, B, and R0 be commutative rings, with B a finite A-module [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft], R0 a Noetherian domain, and A-algebra structures on B and R0. Let F be a field that is a fraction field of R0, with compatible A- and R0-algebra structures. Write m0 for the tensor map B tensor_A R0 to B tensor_A F induced by R0 to F. There exists t in R0, t nonzero, such that for every x in B tensor_A R0, if m0(x) is nilpotent, then (1 tensor t)x is nilpotent.

proof.text: Equip C=B tensor_A R0 with its right R0-algebra structure, and D=B tensor_A F with its C-algebra structure induced by the canonical tensor map m. Mathlib IsLocalization.tensorProduct_tensorProduct_right identifies D as localization of C at images of nonzero elements of R0. If m(x) is nilpotent, choose n with m(x)^n=0. IsLocalization.map_eq_zero_iff gives a nonzero a in R0 with (1 tensor a)x^n=0. For n>0, multiply by (1 tensor a)^(n-1) to show ((1 tensor a)x)^n=0. For n=0 the relation says 1 tensor a=0, so (1 tensor a)x=0.

Let Q=C/nilradical(C), J=m^(-1)(nilradical(D)), and N=J.map(q), where q:C to Q is the quotient map. Tensor commRight and Module.Finite.base_change show that C is finite over R0. Therefore Q and N are finite over the Noetherian ring R0. Every z in N is q(x) for an x in J by Ideal.mem_map_iff_of_surjective. The preceding calculation gives a nonzero a killing z. Thus N is a torsion R0-module.

Apply Submodule.annihilator_top_inter_nonZeroDivisors to the finite torsion module N. It yields t in the annihilator of N and in the nonzero divisors of R0, hence t is nonzero. For any generically nilpotent x, q(x) lies in N, so q((1 tensor t)x)=t smul q(x)=0. Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem and mem_nilradical give the conclusion. The zero algebra and the zero kernel are included in this argument.
